# Navbar

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

navigation and disclosure · tier 2 · beta · renders on the server, with only its interactive part in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For the bar at the top of a site: the brand, the main links and one or two actions. It
stays in view while the page scrolls, and every link is a real anchor in the server HTML.

```ts
import { NavbarActions, NavbarBrand, NavbarLink, NavbarLinks, NavbarRoot } from 'topclassui'
```

```tsx
<NavbarRoot>
  <NavbarBrand href="/">TopClass UI</NavbarBrand>
  <NavbarLinks>
    <NavbarLink href="/docs" current>Docs</NavbarLink>
    <NavbarLink href="/components">Components</NavbarLink>
  </NavbarLinks>
  <NavbarActions>
    <Button render={<a href="/login" />}>Sign in</Button>
  </NavbarActions>
</NavbarRoot>
```

In Next.js, pass the framework link as `render`:

```tsx
<NavbarLink render={<Link href="/docs" />} current>Docs</NavbarLink>
```

- **Parts.** Five flat names and no bare `Navbar`: `NavbarRoot` (a `<header>`),
  `NavbarBrand`, `NavbarLinks` (a `<nav>` holding a list), `NavbarLink` (a list item and its
  link) and `NavbarActions`. Each passes the rest of its props to the element it draws;
  `NavbarLink` passes them to the link.
- **`render`.** On `NavbarBrand` and `NavbarLink`. An element only, never a function.
- **The page being read.** `current` on one `NavbarLink` sets `aria-current="page"`. The
  link is heavier and darker, and underlined too under forced colours. On a narrow screen
  the list opens scrolled to it, so the mark is in view; a browser without
  `scroll-initial-target` opens the list at its start.
- **Sticky.** On by default. `sticky={false}` lets the bar scroll away, and then it sends
  no JavaScript to the browser.
- **What sticky does.** One small client part writes the height of the bar to
  `--tc-sticky-top` on `<html>`. The tokens file reads it into `scroll-padding`, so an
  `#anchor` target, or a link that Tab reaches, stops below the bar and not under it. It
  follows the bar when the bar wraps, and it is removed when the bar unmounts.
- **Before the script runs** the variable is `0px`. A page opened at `/docs#install` lands
  with that heading under the bar (60 px under, measured) and stays there until the reader
  follows another link. To avoid it, give the height in your own CSS:
  `:root { --tc-sticky-top: 3.75rem }`. The bar replaces it with the measured value.
- **One sticky bar a page.** Two would write the same variable: give the second one
  `sticky={false}`.
- **A page that scrolls inside a box.** The window reads the variable by itself. A box of
  your own does not: give it `scroll-padding-top: var(--tc-sticky-top)`.
- **A narrow screen.** Nothing is hidden and nothing is cut. The links scroll sideways
  inside the bar; when the brand and the actions leave them less than 6rem, the actions
  drop to a second row. The page itself never scrolls sideways.
- **Keyboard.** Every link is a tab stop. The link that has the focus is brought whole
  into view inside the list.
- **A name.** `NavbarLinks` is named "Main", from `labels.navbar.label`. With two on a
  page, give one an `aria-label`: yours wins.
- **Arabic.** Pass `labels={ar}` to `NavbarLinks`. The direction comes from `dir` on the
  page: the brand sits at the right and the actions at the left.
- **Long text.** A brand longer than the bar ends in an ellipsis. A label is cut at 100
  characters.
- **Scrollbar.** A desktop browser with classic scrollbars shows one under the links while
  they do not fit.
- **Reduced motion.** Nothing in the bar moves, so there is nothing to reduce.
- **From a server page.** Every part you import is a Server Component: pass text and
  elements.

### What Base UI gives

Nothing: Navbar uses no Base UI part. It is plain HTML and one effect.

### Not built

The mobile menu (the AdaptiveNav connector, a later phase), the scrolled shadow, the
transparent variant, `size`, `bordered`, and a search part: put an `Input` in
`NavbarActions`, as `dummy/with-search.tsx` does.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import {
  NavbarRoot,
  NavbarBrand,
  NavbarLinks,
  NavbarLink,
  NavbarActions,
} from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Every prop below is optional and falls back to the default shown.

### NavbarRoot

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The parts, in order: NavbarBrand, NavbarLinks and NavbarActions. Each one is optional. |
| `sticky` | no | `boolean` | `true` | NavbarRoot: the bar stays at the top while the page scrolls, and publishes its height as --tc-sticky-top. |

### NavbarBrand

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The name of the site, with a logo before it if there is one. |
| `render` | no | `ReactElement` | - | The element the brand is drawn as, such as `render={<Link href="/" />}`. A plain anchor without it. |

### NavbarLinks

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The links: one NavbarLink each. |
| `labels` | no | `Labels` | - | The built-in strings; the nav is named by `labels.navbar.label`. Defaults to English. |
| `locale` | no | `string` | - | Accepted so `{...getLabels(locale)}` spreads cleanly. Nothing here formats a number, so it never reaches the element. |

### NavbarLink

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The text of the link. |
| `current` | no | `boolean` | `false` | NavbarLink: the link of the page being read. It sets aria-current="page" and draws the link heavier. |
| `render` | no | `ReactElement` | - | The element the link is drawn as, such as `render={<Link href="/docs" />}`. A plain anchor without it. |

### NavbarActions

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | What sits at the end of the bar: a Button, a search Input, an Avatar. |

Anything else is passed to the element each part draws, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
